scope: Local-only malicious-mail-server Pass 2 over Lizard. Treated the configured TLS-authenticated IMAP/SMTP endpoint as hostile, traced server protocol bytes and message bodies through framing, parser, memory, database, filesystem, subprocess, terminal and native-renderer boundaries, dynamically tested IMAP aggregation, fuzzed IMAP and MIME parsers in release and AddressSanitizer builds, and checked current RustSec advisories. Product source was not modified.
requested_focus: malicious mail server and remote code execution
boundary_decisions: No host RCE claim was retained: parser fuzzing and boundary review found no demonstrated memory corruption, command injection, path injection or renderer-sandbox escape.
The optional unsandboxed system GnuPG provider remains an RCE-capable dependency boundary but requires a separate GnuPG vulnerability and was not counted as a client finding.
notes: This Pass-2 search and P2-A belong only to the independent mail-client index, never the httpd-rs index.

scope: Local-only Pass 3 over the Lizard command-line mail client at 7c1a668. Built the CLI release workspace with the pinned Rust 1.100.0 toolchain, ran the complete lizard-mail-backend and lizard-mail-tui suites, retained the two failing guard tests, bisected the isolated IMAP worker Landlock policy in disposable copies, and probed message ownership/deletion, filter-undo snapshots and isolated-engine startup with the real public API. No remote server or real IP address was used and the reviewed checkout was not modified.
requested_focus: backdoors, data-loss and unintended-deletion bugs, and surprising security-impact behavior
boundary_decisions: P3-A was classified unclassified rather than denial_of_service: the trigger is host capability, not attacker input, and the control fails closed; the ontology reserves denial_of_service for attacker-triggerable consumption.

P3-B is a confirmed failing guard test but was not scored: the missing-worker fallback is the safe uninspectable-archive warning and production package layouts place workers beside the binary or in /usr/libexec.
Filter undo restoring the captured local-folder snapshot and discarding a later manual membership is documented in spec/mail-backend.md and was retained as an observation, not a defect.

A body pin protects cached content from eviction but does not stop removal of the last copy when its owning account or remote instance disappears; the retained ownership matrix found no deletion beyond the documented model.
notes: Pass-3 token and cost accounting covers the single confirmed unique finding; the unscored P3-B observation shares the same search budget.
